title: McNamara–Sagan–Stanley real-rootedness conjecture for the log-concavity transform
statement:
Let $\{a_k\}$ be a finite sequence of positive real numbers, and define

$$
P[\{a_k\};x]=a_0+a_1x+\cdots+a_nx^n.
$$

Let $\mathfrak{L}(\{a_k\})=\{a_k^2-a_{k-1}a_{k+1}\}$. **McNamara–Sagan–Stanley real-rootedness conjecture.** If $P[\{a_k\};x]$ has only real roots, then $P[\mathfrak{L}(\{a_k\});x]$ also has only real roots. The conjecture proposes that real-rootedness is preserved by the log-concavity transform, strengthening the usual implication from real-rootedness to log-concavity; the source gives no resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3374

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2008).
source_name: Victor H. Moll and Dante Manna, “A remarkable sequence of integers”, arXiv:0812.3374 (2008).
